target.title: fix(gateway): accept local file URLs for managed images
target.body:
Closes #103538

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where callers attaching a local image through a `file://` URL would have managed image preparation fail, even though the same image worked when passed as an absolute path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed outgoing image path now carries the already-resolved local filesystem path through display metadata, policy validation, and storage ingestion. Remote URLs and data URLs keep their existing handling, and local-root enforcement is unchanged.

## User Impact

Valid local `file://` image sources can now be attached through managed outgoing image storage. Query strings, fragments, and source paths are not exposed in the resulting display block.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the focused `file URLs` regression failed in all three gateway shards with `ManagedImageAttachmentError: Managed image attachment "dot.png" could not be prepared` (`3 failed`, `123 skipped`).
- After the fix, and again on exact pushed commit `9bde2bbe2a9`, the same regression passes in all three gateway shards (`3 passed`, `123 skipped`):
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts --configLoader runner src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.test.ts -t 'file URLs'`
- The regression covers the existing absolute-path behavior plus a `file://` URL with query and fragment metadata, asserting the managed block uses `dot.png` and leaks none of the source metadata.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.ts src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.test.ts`
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- Fresh pre-submission autoreview: clean after addressing its query/fragment metadata finding.

AI assistance disclosure: Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, tests, and review. I reviewed and understand every change in this pull request.
